rv.q: Directed by Robin Belfield, the production bursts with energy and laughter, nurturing a message of hope for young people of all ages.
It isn’t groundbreaking but it all makes for a lovely afternoon.

Combined with the work of director Robin Belfield, this is one of the strongest pantomimes at the Lyric to date, and celebrates multiple cross-dressed roles, as well as championing a majority female cast.
With strong choreography and musical numbers, it shows that a panto can be traditional and still unafraid to push the form.
So, while it's an entertaining couple of hours, just as Cinderella asks of the prince when he is tasked with balancing the calls of his heart and duty... best "think for yourself" before you go.
It’s cheerful, silly, unapologetic fun and that’s all you could ask for.
It may be missing a little of the chaos and sparkle that makes a top-tier panto, but there are still enough moments that leave us smiling.
It is more of an aesthetic triumph than a fully blown celebration of panto spirit, then.
A talented cast, inspired costumes and potential political mischief are let down by a production that never quite brings the ingredients together.
I would wholeheartedly recommend this production. Matthew Bourne has created something truly special.
If you are going to go to a panto this year, I highly suggest that you put Cinderella at the top of your list.
With bold yet simple set pieces, fun lighting and upbeat numbers, this production is a fabulous introduction to the festive period and a little camp fun for audiences of all ages.
The production sparkles from the moment Ashh Blackwood exuberantly steps on the stage as Buttons, and under Belfield’s nifty direction this version of Cinderella bounces along.
Cinderella at the Lyric Hammersmith is everything you would expect from a panto.
The song choices mostly work well, with 'Girl on Fire' being a particular highlight, and there are some genuinely entertaining moments throughout.
Clever, gloriously camp and politically irreverent, it knows exactly what it is doing.
Ultimately, this felt like a bit of a stunted start to the festive season.

cn.t: Lyric Hammersmith's Cinderella earns mostly warm notices for its camp energy, political wit, and strong performances, though some find the script uneven. A crowd-pleasing panto with a queer, contemporary twist.
